title: CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT · EMER DESCENT

alert.trigger: Climb or descent: cabin altitude above the higher of 9 550 ft or airfield pressure altitude + 1 000 ft. Cruise: cabin altitude above 9 550 ft.

effectivity.note: The ECAM, memory items and QRH are the same for every HS-TX (Applicable to ALL). Only OEB 61 differs: it applies to HS-TXA..TXF.

summary: A red warning that the cabin altitude is too high. Above FL 160 the crew first does the EMER DESCENT memory items: oxygen masks, signs, descent with AP and A/THR, speed brakes. Then they do the ECAM read-and-do. Without structural damage they descend at maximum speed to FL 100 or MEA/MORA. Below FL 160 they apply the ECAM and start a normal descent.

procedures.title: CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT — ECAM procedure

lines.text: Significantly increases VLS; let speed increase before using speed brakes to avoid AP disconnection and speed-brake retraction by AoA protection.
If structural damage is suspected, use the flight controls with care and reduce speed; with L/G extended, reduce to VLO/VLE.
Squawk 7700 unless otherwise specified by ATC.
To save oxygen, set the oxygen diluter selector to N position. With the oxygen diluter left to 100 %, oxygen quantity may not be sufficient for the entire descent profile.
Confirms that the passenger oxygen masks are released.

When descent is established, and if time permits, check that the OUTFLOW VALVES are closed on the CAB PRESS SD page. If they are not closed and ΔP is positive, select the other CPC. If the OUTFLOW VALVE is still not closing, set the cabin pressure MODE SEL pb to MAN and adjust the V/S CTL sw, according to the table.

procedures.title: OEB 61 — CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT

lines.text: Apply the CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT ECAM procedure, even if not confirmed on the CAB PRESS SD page.

tables.title: Manual cabin pressure targets
tables.caption: TGT V/S: CLIMB 500 ft/min, DESC 300 ft/min (if MODE SEL MAN is needed).

background.text: Depressurization is identified by excessive and uncontrollable cabin altitude and rate of climb, the CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT alert, or all cabin oxygen masks dropping (independent pressure switch).
At idle, high speed and speed brakes out, the descent rate is about 7 000 ft/min: FL 390 to FL 100 takes about 4 min and 40 NM.
Suspect structural damage after a loud bang or a high cabin V/S.
OEB 61 root cause: the active CPC can show a wrong but normal-looking cabin altitude; the standby CPC triggers the alert. The crew may wrongly disregard the alert or delay the descent.

technique.text: Above FL 160: EMER DESCENT memory items first, then the ECAM. Below FL 160: ECAM procedure and a normal descent.
Two steps: memory items (PM monitors the FMA), then read & do (PF adjusts the settings).
At high levels, extend speed brakes while monitoring VLS so AoA protection does not retract them or disconnect the AP.
Structural damage suspected: SPEED/MACH pb to SPEED to stop the IAS increasing or to reduce speed; use speed brakes carefully.
Below FL 100 limit the descent rate to about 1 000 ft/min (PDP adds 500 ft/min for passenger comfort), except on approach.

related.title: CAB PR SYS 1+2 FAULT
related.why: Both CPCs failed — a common lead-in to the excess cabin altitude
key_actions: MAN V/S CTL AS RQRD; keep aircraft altitude at or above cabin altitude
Final approach: V/S CTL FULL UP; ΔP zero before opening doors

values.HS-TXA..TXF: Applies: do the ECAM even if the CAB PRESS SD page looks normal

gaps.text: The ECAM has no explicit LAND ASAP for this alert; the diversion decision follows the general assess/decide step.
Callout wording comes from the PDP; the FCOM memory-item callout is “EMERGENCY DESCENT”.
The PDP says the EMER DESCENT (PA) line may not show on the ECAM on some aircraft; it is in the HS-TX FCOM procedure.
